summary:
AGRO MESH is a voice-first, offline-capable farm planning tool that helps farmers build and compare five-year crop rotations. It combines NASA POWER observations with weather forecasts, soil data, crop characteristics, and the farmer’s priorities. Farmers can weigh water savings, soil recovery, and profit against practical constraints such as available labor and equipment. Each plan explains why crops were selected and estimates trade-offs in irrigation demand, nitrogen credits, and farm margins.

The project addresses the challenge by turning scientific data into decisions farmers can discuss in plain language. With the local models installed and data cached, farmers can ask questions by voice, compare strategies, and hear recommendations even when internet access is unreliable.

Crop rotations affect soil health, water use, and income for years. AGRO MESH helps farmers see those trade-offs before committing a season’s seed, labor, and irrigation budget.
details:
AGRO MESH is a voice-first farm planning application built for growers who need to make crop rotation and irrigation decisions with limited connectivity. A farmer can set up a field, choose priorities such as water conservation, soil recovery, or profit, and ask for a five-year rotation in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.

The rotation engine compares crop families, seasonal planting windows, water demand, nitrogen contributions, equipment and labor needs, and projected margins. NASA POWER supplies weather and solar radiation data, while other sources add forecasts, soil properties, and elevation. The application explains its recommendations in plain language and shows where each input came from. Farmers can also compare 1,000 simulated financial scenarios and generate a compact field alert for a simulated Mesh relay.

We built the prototype with Python, FastAPI, SQLite, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Leaflet. Vosk handles local speech recognition, Ollama runs the conversational model, and Piper provides offline text-to-speech. After the models are installed and observations are cached, the core workflow runs on a laptop without internet access. A standard microphone and speakers support the voice interface.

The creative contribution is the connection between conversation and practical decisions. A farmer can ask what changes if water becomes scarce, hear the trade-offs, and immediately see the resulting rotation. We considered unreliable connectivity, regional differences in data coverage, forecast uncertainty, and the need to distinguish measured inputs from modeled estimates. The intended impact is to help farmers plan for soil health, water use, and financial risk before committing resources to a season.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

OpenAI Codex assisted with drafting, debugging, and testing the application code. Ollama runs a local language model that interprets questions, selects application tools, and explains results. Piper generates synthetic narration offline, and optional ElevenLabs integration generates synthetic narration online. NASA and partner observations come from their original providers. Modeled projections and simulated demonstration readings are identified separately.

How AGRO MESH uses it

NASA POWER

Queries and caches temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation for planning.

NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS)

Serves satellite map layers, including Terra MODIS and SMAP.

Terra MODIS

Displays true-color imagery and monthly NDVI through GIBS.

Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP)

Displays a regional root-zone soil moisture layer and accepts dated numeric imports.

Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM)

Uses SRTM elevation samples through OpenTopoData to estimate slope.

GPM IMERG

Supports importing dated precipitation observations for alert and road-risk screening.

ECOSTRESS

Supports importing dated land-surface temperature observations for heat alerts.

NASA Land Data Assimilation Systems (NLDAS / GLDAS)

Supports importing soil-moisture observations with provenance.

You can see a demo with a bit more explanation at this YouTube link; it's only 4 minutes long!:

https://youtu.be/JQ8hX4vrB4M?si=NFfoVL_iGPChTEwH
